dedupe_keys.name: brite boston university representative internet topology generator

description: BRITE is a universal topology generator that produces synthetic Internet-like topologies at the router level, the autonomous-system level or both in a hierarchy. It implements several generation models, including Waxman random graphs and Barabási-Albert preferential attachment, with node placement in a plane, bandwidth and delay assignment on links, and exports to the input formats of network simulators such as ns-2, SSFNet, JavaSim and OMNeT++. It was built at Boston University to support research that depends on a realistic understanding of the large-scale structure of the Internet's physical topology; the developers no longer support it, but questions can still go to the brite-users mailing list. Coverage: synthetic graphs of any size the user sets, not tied to real geography. Format and access: Java and C++ implementations with a graphical interface, downloaded from the project page; free of charge for research use. Caveats: unmaintained since the 2000s; its models predate current understanding of Internet topology; outputs are synthetic and must not be read as real networks. Simulation uses: synthetic benchmark topologies for network flow, capacity planning, cascading-failure and resilience experiments. Related records: CAIDA ITDK and AS relationships give measured topologies, SNDlib gives real backbone instances, and CloudSim can load BRITE files.
